messages:
tara: Heads up — after rolling int4 on the mistralx-14b variant for chat/summarize we see a quality delta on multi-turn summarization sets. Short repro attached. :thinking_face:

ravi: ack. numbers?

tara: quick summary:
- fp16 baseline ROUGE-L: 38.2
- int4 quant (group=128, per-channel symmetric) ROUGE-L: 34.7
- delta -3.5 absolute, increases with >3 turns
- latency down ~2.3x on the same GPU (expected)

mika: do you have the eval split? is it dialogue summarization or single-doc?

tara: multi-turn customer support snippets, 3-8 turns, average 120 tokens context. Eval harness: eval-bot/conv-sum-v2. Repro script posted below.

tara: ```
# quantize and run eval (condensed)
python quantize.py --model mistralx-14b --bits 4 --group-size 128 --per-channel symmetric --out q_mx14b/
python run_eval.py --model q_mx14b/ --task conv-sum-v2 --batch 8 --kv-cache true
```

devx-sam: can you paste an example where int4 hallucinated or diverged?

tara: short example:
- user: "we canceled order 12345, what is status?"
- fp16 summary: "Order 12345 was canceled on 2026-01-12; refund processed to card ending 4242; ETA 3–5 business days."
- int4 summary: "Order 12345 is scheduled for delivery tomorrow; tracking 9400..." (wrong)

ravi: hmm interesting. sounds like either tokenization or kv-cache misalignment (rotary scaling mismatch can manifest mid-context). Did you change rotary params during export/compile?

tara: we used the standard export flow: convert -> quantize -> compile. No manual rotary tweaks. I dumped logits at step boundaries, saw gradual drift after ~20 tokens in the same prompt.

mika: what about tokenizer normalization? some examples include em-dash vs hyphen, and int4 might make rare-token logits noisier causing OOV-like mapping. Try NFKC normalizing and rerun.

tara: did a quick run with nfkc on; marginal improvement +0.3 ROUGE-L only. Not the root cause.

eval-bot: automated metrics from latest run (timestamp 2614099800):
- avg ROUGE-L fp16: 38.2
- avg ROUGE-L int4: 34.7
- exact match of named entities (order IDs) fp16: 92% -> int4: 73%
- hallucination rate (asserts wrong dates/ids) fp16: 3% -> int4: 12%

ravi: that entity drop is a red flag. Could be token id remapping issue during quantize or a subtle token embedding reorder. Check vocabulary mapping between exported fp16 and quantized artefacts. Did hashes/ordinals shift?

tara: mapping file shows identical size and ordering in our converter manifest, but I saw a few duplicate tokens in the quantized embedding table at positions ~5021-5026 (small cluster). Could that happen with aggressive per-channel symmetric packing?

mika: duplicates could be a write-time bug in the quantizer -> embedding axes transposed. Try run: python inspect_embeddings.py --model q_mx14b/ --check-duplicates --dump-positions 5000-5050

tara: ran it. Output: two identical rows at 5023 and 5024 (cosine=0.9998). fp16 rows there are distinct (cosine ~0.02).

devx-sam: aha. that explains entity collapse (different tokens mapping to the same embedding). Likely corruption in the quantize step when writing float->packed-int. Which quantizer tool? our internal qpack v2?

tara: qpack v2 + our compile pipeline. I reproduced by quantizing only the embedding matrix and loading the compiled model — same symptom.

ravi: create minimal repro: quantize only embeddings with same config and run a tiny eval on detects for tokens around that region. If repro holds isolate quantize code path. Also try group-size 64 and per-tensor to see if cluster disappears.

tara: quick matrix:
- group=128, per-channel symmetric -> duplicates present -> ROUGE-L 34.7
- group=64, per-channel -> duplicates reduced, ROUGE-L 36.5
- per-tensor symmetric -> no duplicates, ROUGE-L 37.9

mika: so the per-channel symmetric pack algorithm likely has an off-by-one when group-size aligns with embedding dim. Maybe floor/ceil mismatch when slicing final group.

ravi: assign to eng-ml quant team to triage qpack v2 group slicing. Label: quant/bug/emb-dup-5023. Tara, please attach the exact quantize config and a minimal dump file (emb rows 5016-5032) to the ticket.

tara: created ticket QUANT-1749 and attached dump + eval logs. Also adding a temporary mitigation: use per-tensor or group-size 64 for production until patch. Rolling patch to staging now.

devx-sam: for rollout policy, recommend canary 1% with fallback to fp16 model in case hallucination rate >7% on sampled queries. Add automatic alert in console when named-entity EM drops >10 points.

ravi: also add a unit test in quant pack that compares per-channel rolled statistics against fp16 baseline after packing/unpacking on random seeds. Should catch transposition/dup issues.

mika: and add a small embedding-consistency smoke check to the compile pipeline: sample 100 tokens, compare cosine similarity of embeddings pre/post quantize and fail build if >3 tokens below 0.6 similarity.

tara: noted. I'll add those to the ticket. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

ravi: one last thought — check if tokenizer uses fallback merges causing token IDs near 5023 to be overloaded by subword merges. But given fp16 is fine and per-tensor fixes it, quantizer bug is most likely.

tara: agreed. I'll follow up with a postmortem once QUANT-1749 is resolved and we run a full regression over conv-sum-v2 + longform-news.
